attribute_pattern.document.en: it carries text columns ({columns}) and nothing refers to it

attribute_pattern.event.en: it is dated ({column}) and points at {targets}

attribute_pattern.organisation.en: it carries a name that is not personal ({column}) with a place or a contact

attribute_pattern.person.en: it carries personal columns that name a human ({columns})

attribute_pattern.product.en: other concepts refer to it ({sources}) and its key names a thing

different_parents.en: they belong to different values of {level} ({a}, {b})

functional_dependency.all.en: in all {objects} objects that carry both, each {a} goes with exactly one {b}

functional_dependency.most.en: over {objects} objects, {holding} of {checked} values of {a} go with exactly one {b}

key_contains_key.en: the key of {concept} ({key}) contains the key of {whole} ({columns})

key_contains_part_of_key.en: the key of {concept} ({key}) contains {columns}, one column of the key of {whole}

language_model.class.en: proposed by {model} as a class between concepts and {parent}

language_model.declined.en: {model} found none of the classes fitting

metric_view_dimension.en: named “{label}” as a dimension of a metric view

metric_view_measure.en: a measure of the metric view {view}

name.same_core.en: the same name apart from the legal form

name.token_share.en: the names share {percent}% of their distinctive words

name_and_inclusion.column.en: {child}.{column} is named like the key {parent}.{key} and its values are found there

name_and_inclusion.key.en: {child} carries ({columns}), the key of {parent}, and its values are found there

name_and_inclusion.part_of_key.en: {child}.{column} is named after {parent} and is one column of its key ({key}); its values are found there

names_an_entity.en: {value_set} has {values} values over the {keys} rows of {entity}: it names a single {entity}, it does not group them

refers_to_a_level.all.en: each row of {concept} carries one {level}, which is a level of a hierarchy

refers_to_a_level.some.en: {filled} of {rows} rows of {concept} carry a {level}, which is a level of a hierarchy; the others sit under none

same_grouping.en: in all {objects} objects that carry both, each {a} goes with exactly one {b} and each {b} with exactly one {a}

same_key.en: a derived object with the key of {base} ({key})

shared_column.value_set.en: the column {column} appears in {objects} objects with at most {values} distinct values

top_class.document.definition.en: A text someone wrote and filed: a bulletin, a report, a letter.

top_class.event.definition.en: Something that happened at a time and involves other things: a claim, a visit, a recall.

top_class.organisation.definition.en: A company, a public body or a unit of one that acts under a name.

top_class.person.definition.en: A human being. Records of persons are never shown.

top_class.place.definition.en: A location or an area: a town, a region, a market.

top_class.product.definition.en: A thing that is made, sold, owned or repaired, or a kind of such things.

unique_key.combination.en: ({columns}): a combination unique in the data, over {rows} rows

unique_key.join_target.en: ({columns}): the target of a metric-view join, unique in the data, over {rows} rows

unique_key.own_name.en: ({columns}): named after the object, unique in the data, over {rows} rows

unique_key.unique.en: ({columns}): unique in the data, over {rows} rows

verified_join.en: verified by the host's layer job
